articles.title: Sea Anemones Flip the Script on Antiviral Defense
articles.summary: A newly discovered protein in sea anemones, CARDIB, suppresses the immune system to fight viruses—the opposite of a crucial human protein. This challenges the idea that all animals share a single antiviral strategy. The finding, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, reveals evolution found multiple solutions to viral threats.

articles.title: Hubble Captures Ancient Stellar Sparkler for America's 250th
articles.summary: To mark the U.S. 250th anniversary, NASA released a Hubble image of globular cluster NGC 6426. The 13-billion-year-old cluster, located in the Milky Way's halo, glitters with red, white, and blue stars. Its ancient stars offer clues about the early universe and galaxy formation.

articles.title: Alzheimer's Spread May Rely on a Brain Protein's Double Life
articles.summary: A study in Cell reveals that the brain protein Arc, normally involved in cell communication, also enables toxic Tau to spread between neurons in Alzheimer's. Removing Arc in mice halted Tau transfer. The finding suggests a new treatment strategy: blocking Tau's travel rather than eliminating it.
